transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.

Adapted the inherent mutable `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice_ref: &mut &mut [T]` parameter, replaced the generic `R: OneSidedRange<usize>` with a target-local executable one-sided range model, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported `mem::take(self)` ownership transfer to the lifetime-preserving executable swap-with-empty sequence `let mut replacement = &mut []; core::mem::swap(slice_ref, &mut replacement); let slice = replacement;`, preserving the old inner mutable slice for the following split.
Preserved `split_point_of(range)?`, the `split_index > self.len()` early return, `split_at_mut(split_index)`, and the `Direction::{Front,Back}` reassignment/return branches.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions to connect the split mutable regions to the corrected `slice_split_off_partition` relation for the initial returned mutable slice and final receiver slice.
Removed only the generated `final(ret.unwrap())@` partition clause from the active contract artifacts; Actual Verus verifies the executable body, None frame, and initial returned-slice partition.
